intro.title: Functions — Arrow, Closures & HOF
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple program that uses different types of functions to manage a list of tasks. You will learn how to write arrow functions for concise expressions, create closures to encapsulate data, and apply higher-order functions to transform arrays. The core concepts covered are function definitions, lexical scoping, and function composition. You will work with JavaScript's built-in array methods like map and filter. By the end, you'll understand how to combine these techniques to write cleaner and more powerful code.
intro.usecase: Arrow functions, closures, and higher-order functions are essential patterns in modern JavaScript applications. You'll use them when building interactive dashboards that filter data, creating form validation with reusable logic, or implementing dynamic UI components like modals and menus. For example, when handling user events in a shopping cart, closures maintain item state while arrow functions provide clean callback syntax. These patterns enable modular, maintainable code in real-world scenarios like API response processing, user authentication flows, and real-time data updates.
